title.narrative: Strengthening the livelihoods of vulnerable populations affected by extreme climate change events in the far north of Cameroon

description.narrative: With the aim of strengthening the resilience of beneficiary populations to climatic shocks, the main agropastoral activities will be developed over the project period. These are as follows- Agricultural support for market-garden production: Market-garden production will be carried out on an area of 1,000 m2 per household, i.e. a total area of households, i.e. a total area of 85 ha to be planted by 850 households (5,100 beneficiaries), for a total production of 949,200 kg of leafy vegetables and fruit vegetables, i.e. an average production of 1,200 kg perhousehold. The inputs will include seed of early varieties, watering can, machete, hoe, daba hoe, daba, bio-pesticide, string and sprayer to produce high-value crops with high nutritional value (guinea sorrel, nightshade, tomato tomato) for household consumption from 6 weeks, and for up to up to 16 weeks.- Agricultural support for rain-fed production: Rain-fed production for a household of 6 people will be developed on 3/4 of a hectare, and will cover food needs in cereals. As well as legumes, in particular cowpeas, are used in the diet, 1/4 hectare will be devoted is devoted to it. In total, for a household of 6 people, the project's support will focus on the distribution of 16 kg of seed per household, comprising 6 kg of sorghum, 5 kg of maize and 5 kg of cowpea. Each household will also receive 3 hoes, a sprayer for 10 growers and biopesticide for the treatment of cowpea.biopesticide for cowpea treatment. A total of 750 households will be assisted to produce their own cereal and legume food.- Poultry support: The project will support beneficiaries by providing them with modern poultry houses that will reduce the incidence of recurrent poultry diseases in the community. These higher-quality inputs will enable chickens weighing 2.5 to 3 kg to be produced in a maximum of two months, helping beneficiaries to boost their income and increase their consumption of animal protein in order to improve their food and nutritional security. The project includes the provision of 21-day-old chickens (50), a modern henhouse, growth feed, veterinary products, drinking troughs and feeders for the production of broilers ready for consumption after 7 to 9 weeks of rearing. A total of 50 households (300 beneficiaries)- Support for fish farming: The project will support households with production inputs (juvenile fish weighing at least 150 g and feed in the form of floating pellets of varying sizes depending on the age of the fish), and sustainable production infrastructure (above-ground tanks). After 03 months of rearing, households will be able to collect fish with an average weight of around 600 g, enabling them to meet their nutritional needs and strengthen their food security. It should also be noted that the choice of the catfish species (Clarias gariapinus) for this project is based on the quality and quantity of its flesh, which makes it a species suitable for children's nutrition and health. Beneficiary households will receive a 2 m3 above-ground tank (01), Clarias fry (300), landing net (01), digital pH and aquatic thermometer (01), Clarias 2 mm 45% feed (04 bags of 15 kg), Clarias 3 mm feed (7 bags of 15 kg), Clarias 4.5 mm feed (7 bags of 15 kg), Clarias 6 mm feed (5 bags of 15 kg). A total of 150 households (900 people) will benefit from the intervention.- Capacity-building support for local stakeholders: To ensure the sustainability of the project, 55 local stakeholders will be trained in agropastoral and fish farming techniques adapted to extreme climatic conditions. The aim of these trained actors will be to provide local support to project beneficiaries in sustainable production related to agriculture, poultry and fish farming beyond the project intervention period. This intervention will have positive short- and medium-term effects on food security, and will strengthen sources of income for beneficiary households.
